query:
DECLARE @lastRunTimestampUTC DATETIMEOFFSET = CAST('{{{timestamp}}}' AS DATETIMEOFFSET);
DECLARE @lastRunTimestampMEZ DATETIME2 = 
    CONVERT(datetime2, @lastRunTimestampUTC AT TIME ZONE 'Central European Standard Time');

SELECT
    O.Tour AS tour_set_name,
    O.STATUS_KEY AS tour_state_id,
    O.UPDATE_TS AS tour_update_ts,    
    OP.OrderID AS vbeln,
    CASE
        WHEN OP.QUANTITY_MISSING > 0 THEN 'Missing Items'
        WHEN OP.QUANTITY_DONE = OP.QUANTITY THEN 'Completed'
        WHEN OP.QUANTITY_DONE > 0 THEN 'In Progress'
        WHEN OP.QUANTITY_PREPARED = OP.QUANTITY THEN 'Prepared'
        WHEN OP.QUANTITY_PREPARED > 0 THEN 'Partially Prepared'
        ELSE 'Not Started'
    END AS vbeln_state,
    OP.UPDATE_TS AS vbeln_update_ts    
FROM
    [CP_Sorter].[dbo].[T3_ORDER] O
INNER JOIN
    [CP_Sorter].[dbo].[T3_ORDERPOS] OP
    ON O.ORDER_NO = OP.ORDER_NO
WHERE
    O.INSERT_TS > @lastRunTimestampMEZ or
    O.UPDATE_TS > @lastRunTimestampMEZ or
    OP.INSERT_TS > @lastRunTimestampMEZ or
    OP.UPDATE_TS > @lastRunTimestampMEZ
ORDER BY
    O.Tour, OP.OrderID;

name: ER - Error State
info:
If a warning or an error occurs on the cutter this Status Command is sent to the Status Channel.

Syntax 1: ER ErrorNumber;
Syntax 2: ER ErrorNumber, int Index1, int Index2;
Syntax 3: ER ErrorNumber, uint Index1, uint Index2;
Syntax 4: ER ErrorNumber, hex Index1, hex Index2;
Syntax 5: ER ErrorNumber, uint Index1, string Message;

ErrorNumber: Error number of thrown error on cutter.
Attention: The ErrorNumber is sent in hexadecimal format (as shown on panel). To recognize the hexadecimal format there is a leading ‘0x’ at the beginning of the number.
int Index1: Two additional indexes in signed integer format.
int Index2:
uint Index1: Two additional indexes in unsigned integer format.
uint Index2:
hex Index1: Two additional indexes in hexadecimal format. To recognize the hexadecimal
hex Index2: format there is a leading ‘0x’ at the beginning of the number.
uint Index1: One additional index in unsigned integer format, followed by a string which
string Message: contains additional informations.

Example 1: ER 0x0002D802;

Note for Error Categories:
The last number in the hexadecimal code of ErrorNumber defines the error category. There are four categories:
1: User information (not an Error, cutter will not stop or go offline)
2: Warning (There may be a problem, but the cutter will not stop or go offline)
3: Failure (Cutter switches to stopped mode. The user can solve the problem and go online afterwards)
4: Fatal Error (Cutter switches to stopped mode, the user must shutdown cutter)

name: CF - CradleFeeder State
info:
This command reflects changes of the state from the cradle feeder 100/200.

Syntax: CF RollOffReady, FeederOk;

RollOffReady:
0: Feeder not prepared with roll for synchronous roll off.
1: Feeder prepared with roll for synchronous roll off.

FeederOk:
0: Feeder has a problem or is switched off.
1: No problem on feeder.

Example: CF 1, 1;

name: VW - Vacuum Width
ST - Selected Tool
info:
This Status Command reflects every tool change. If a new tool is selected (e.g. by HPGL Command SP) on cutter this command is sent to the Status Channel.

Syntax: ST SelectedTool;
ST SelectedTool, SelectedSlaveTool;

SelectedTool: Actual selected tool
These values are possible: 0: when no module or tool is selected (e.g. while start up) 11,12,13: for tools on module 1 21,22,23: for tools on module 2 31,32,33: for tools on module 3 81: when camera is selected 91: when laser pointer is selected

SelectedSlaveTool: Actual selected slave tool
11,12,13: for tools on module 1
21,22,23: for tools on module 2
31,32,33: for tools on module 3

Example: ST 11; First tool in module 1 is selected.
ST 31, 21;
The first tool in module 3 is selected as master tool and the first tool in module 2 is selected as slave tool.

VS - Vacuum State
info:
This Status Command reflects the state of the vacuum system. On every change on the vacuum system this command is sent to the Status Channel. For tandem systems there may be two vacuum area on a cutter.

Syntax: VS VacuumArea, AreaState, ValveState, BlowingPossible, VacuumLevel;

VacuumArea: Number of vacuum area
0: vacuum front / whole area
1: vacuum rear area

AreaState:
0: area activity off
1: area activity on

ValveState:
0: blowing
1: sucking

BlowingPossible:
0: blowing / aircushion not possible
1: blowing / aircushion possible

VacuumLevel:
0: vacuum level not supported
1 – 10: vacuum level

Example: VS 0, 0, 1, 1, 0;
The front / whole area activity is off. The valve in those area are on sucking (vacuum) position, but it’s also possible to generate an aircushion. Different vacuum levels are not supported (only a turbine can have different vacuum levels).

name: FS - Feed State
info:
This Status Command reflects events of a feed process.

Sometimes it’s necessary to add an additional length to the feed length. For further information have a look at the example for FS11 and also the notes of this command.

Syntax: FS Event, ProceededFeedLength, FeedLength;

Event: Feed event
0: Started
1: Completed
10: Continued
11: Continued without loading material
20: Suspended by the external feed stop signal
30: Stopped
31: Stopped by the external feed stop signal
32: Stopped before feed
33: Stopped after feed
99: Cancelled

ProceededFeedLength: Feed length that has already been proceeded in plotter units [0.01 mm].
FeedLength: Total feed length to proceed in plotter units [0.01 mm].

Example: FS 0, 0, 250000;
The feed process started.
FS 1, 250000, 250000;
The feed process completed successfully.
FS 10, 98721, 160000;
The feed process is continued after a stop.
FS 11, 0, 270400; (feed length 250000, loading offset X 20400)
The user confirmed a dialog on the operating unit which continues the feed process without loading material by a board or a sheet feeder.
FS 20, 121532, 320000;
The feed process is suspended by the external feed stop signal. The feed process is stopped while the signal is pending and will automatically continue when the signal is cleared.
FS 30, -126732, -200000;
The feed process is stopped because of a stop event by the system or by the user.
FS 31, 81565, 250000;
The feed process is stopped by the external feed stop signal.
FS 32, 0, 250000;
The feed process is stopped because of a user setting.
(operating unit 1-7-1-7-1).
FS 33, 0, 250000;
The feed process is stopped because of a user setting.
(operating unit 1-7-1-7-2).
FS 99, -167810, -250000;
The feed process has been cancelled.

Subflow description
info:
# Insert Queue

Process of this subflow:
 1. queue messages
 2. insert message by message into postgresql node
 3. drop the message from the queue, when it was processed succesfull
 4. peek a new message from the queue
 5. repeat

Each input will be queued inside the q-gate node. (FIFO)
During start of the subflow a Trigger will be activated. This trigger will send a "control: peek" message at a given interval.
This is necessary because when the queue is empty we need to periodically check if a new message is available.
When a message is dequeued the trigger will be deactivated (msg.reset: true) until the message is processed by the postgresql node.
